live.title: DevOps Engineer
live.summary: Automate the path from code to production: Linux, Bash and Python, networking, containers, pipelines, Kubernetes, infrastructure as code, cloud and monitoring.
live.audience: Sysadmins, developers and support engineers moving into DevOps roles.
outcomes: Administer and troubleshoot Linux servers from the command line.
Automate routine work with safe, readable Bash scripts.
Package applications as small, secure container images.
Build CI/CD pipelines with tests, artifacts and staged deployments.
Deploy and debug workloads on Kubernetes.
Provision infrastructure with Terraform and keep state safe.
Add metrics, logs and alerts so you know when a release hurts users.
Write Python and Bash automation that talks to APIs and cloud SDKs.
Operate across AWS and Azure well enough to deploy a full stack.
Keep fleets of servers consistent with Ansible inventories, playbooks and roles.
Operate relational databases: indexes, backups, replication and safe schema changes.
Use Git daily: branches, merges, rebase, pull requests, tags and recovery with the reflog.

live.title: Cloud Engineer
live.summary: Design and run cloud infrastructure on AWS and Azure with networking, identity, Terraform, serverless, containers and monitoring.
live.audience: Engineers who build and operate infrastructure in public cloud accounts.
outcomes: Explain the shared responsibility model and apply least-privilege identity.
Design virtual networks with public and private subnets on AWS and Azure.
Choose between virtual machines, containers and serverless for a workload.
Provision and change cloud resources safely with Terraform.
Run managed Kubernetes and ship to it from a pipeline.
Track cost and apply well-architected practices.
Build serverless and managed Kubernetes workloads, and secure them with governance controls.
Script cloud tasks with Python and the CLI.
Run managed and self-hosted databases with backups, failover and tested restores.

live.title: Site Reliability Engineer
live.summary: Keep services reliable: Linux, containers and cloud first, then observability, SLOs, on-call, incident response, capacity and chaos testing.
live.audience: Operations and platform engineers who own uptime and on-call.
outcomes: Debug performance and failures on Linux and in Kubernetes.
Instrument services and write alerts that page for symptoms, not noise.
Define SLIs and SLOs, and use error budgets to guide release decisions.
Run an incident with clear roles, communication and a timeline.
Write blameless postmortems that lead to real fixes.
Find toil and replace it with automation.
Run a healthy on-call rotation and plan capacity before it runs out.
Practise failure with game days and manage change safely.
Reason about database failure modes, recovery targets and safe change rollouts.

live.title: DevSecOps Engineer
live.summary: Secure delivery from code to cloud: pipeline and supply chain controls, hardened containers and clusters, secrets, cloud identity and security incident response.
live.audience: DevOps, platform and security engineers who own the safety of what ships.
outcomes: Run a threat modeling session and turn findings into tracked work.
Keep secrets out of code and images, and use short-lived credentials.
Add dependency, code, infrastructure and image scanning to a pipeline with sensible gates.
Produce an SBOM and sign artifacts so deployments can verify them.
Harden containers and Kubernetes workloads with least privilege and network policies.
Design least-privilege cloud identity and protect audit logs.
Prioritise vulnerabilities by real risk and meet agreed fix times.
Lead the first hour of a security incident while preserving evidence.
Protect automation secrets with Vault and keep database backups, access and migrations safe.

live.title: AI Engineer
live.summary: Build with large language models: how they work, prompting and structured output, Claude Skills, and tool use with the Model Context Protocol, on top of Linux, Git, Python and networking.
live.audience: Developers and DevOps engineers who want to build, package and operate AI features safely.
outcomes: Explain tokens, context windows, sampling and why models make mistakes.
Call a model API with sensible limits, retries, streaming and cost control.
Write prompts with clear roles, examples and constraints, and test them like code.
Get structured JSON from a model and validate, repair or reject it.
Package repeatable expertise as a Claude Skill with a description that triggers reliably.
Test, version and review skills before sharing them with a team.
Define tools with schemas and run the tool-use loop correctly.
Build a small MCP server and defend it against prompt injection and over-broad permissions.

live.title: MLOps and AIOps Engineer
live.summary: Run machine learning and algorithm-assisted operations in production: containers and Kubernetes, pipelines, observability, then MLOps and AIOps.
live.audience: DevOps and SRE engineers who support data science teams, and data engineers who need production habits.
outcomes: Explain how ML systems fail quietly and what to monitor.
Validate and version data and features, and avoid leakage.
Track experiments so any model can be reproduced.
Build a training pipeline with tests and an evaluation gate.
Release models with a registry, shadow runs, canaries and rollback.
Serve models in batch, online or streaming modes with sensible limits.
Detect drift and retrain safely.
Use anomaly detection, alert correlation and incident hints without losing human judgement.
Automate routine fixes with limits, verification and a kill switch.
Build change correlation and topology-aware root cause hints, and measure them against real incidents.
Run agents and remediation safely with approval tiers, audit trails, kill switches and prompt injection defences.

live.title: Platform Engineer
live.summary: Build internal developer platforms: golden paths, self-service infrastructure, a developer portal, guardrails and the measures that show developers are better off.
live.audience: DevOps, SRE and cloud engineers who want to build the shared platform other engineering teams use, and developers moving into platform work.
outcomes: Explain what a platform is, who it serves and how it differs from DevOps and SRE.
Run the platform as a product: find user pain, rank it, ship the thinnest useful slice and measure adoption.
Design golden paths with sensible defaults and documented exits.
Model services, owners and dependencies in a catalog and keep it accurate.
Build self-service workflows that validate input, apply policy and leave an audit trail.
Offer infrastructure through declarative platform APIs instead of tickets.
Apply guardrails, secure defaults and policy as code without blocking developers.
Provide isolated environments, previews and tenants, and clean them up.
Allocate cost to teams and report unit costs.
Measure developer experience with delivery metrics, onboarding time and surveys.
Set platform SLOs, run support and on-call, and plan adoption, migration and deprecation.

live.title: Kubernetes Administrator (CKA)
live.summary: The first end goal: build, upgrade, back up and troubleshoot clusters, with deep dives on the control plane, networking and resources, then exam practice.
live.audience: Engineers preparing for the CKA who want to learn how clusters really work and practise under realistic conditions.
outcomes: Design and bootstrap a highly available cluster with kubeadm and keep its certificates current.
Upgrade a cluster one minor version at a time, and drain, replace and rejoin nodes safely.
Back up and restore etcd, and rehearse a full recovery.
Explain the request path, etcd, the scheduler, controllers and the kubelet well enough to diagnose each.
Set requests, limits, quotas and autoscaling from measurement, and plan for disruption.
Explain the pod network, Services, DNS and policies, and debug them in a fixed order.
Expose applications with Services, Ingress and the Gateway API.
Provision and debug persistent storage.
Work quickly and accurately in a timed, performance-based exam.

live.title: Kubernetes Security Specialist (CKS)
live.summary: The second end goal: the full CKA path, then pipeline and platform security, a Kubernetes security deep dive and exam practice.
live.audience: Administrators who hold or are working toward the CKA and now want to harden clusters, workloads and supply chains.
outcomes: Everything in the CKA path, as the foundation.
Model threats to a cluster and place a control at each step of an attack.
Design least privilege RBAC and audit who can do what.
Enforce Pod Security and admission policy, and encrypt secrets at rest.
Isolate tenants with namespaces, policies, quotas and sandboxed runtimes.
Harden the API server and kubelet against the CIS benchmark.
Scan images, restrict registries and detect runtime threats with audit logs and Falco.
Contain, investigate and recover from a compromised cluster.
Work quickly and accurately in a timed, performance-based exam.

planned.title: FinOps and cloud cost
planned.summary: Measure, allocate and reduce cloud spend without hurting reliability.

planned.title: Data platform engineer
planned.summary: Build pipelines, storage and governance for analytics and machine learning teams.

planned.title: Network automation engineer
planned.summary: Automate switches, routers and cloud networks with code, templates and tests.
